name: Maison Kitsuné
why: Paris label and record company from 2002, the Fox Head on tees and sweatshirts, made mostly in Portugal; 63 boutiques abroad and none in the US.
origin: Founded in 2002 (not stated on the pages read; inferred from the about page "for the past nineteen years" on a 2021-copyright page and the house's own "Maison Kitsuné 2002" tees; confirm) in Paris, France ("Independent Paris fashion house", about page) by Gildas Loaëc and Masaya Kuroki (founders page).

marks: unbranded only: "water-repellent" nylon/polyester on the quilted puffers and jackets, "water-repellent technical canvas" on the cargo pants, "technical cotton and nylon blend" windbreaker
no named membrane, insulation or performance fibre

craft_evidence.owned: claim only: the Savoir-Faire page says the capsule is "designed between our Paris atelier and Japan" and the leather jacket is "handcrafted in Paris"; no factory or workshop is named or shown as owned; the PDP traceability text says collections are produced "by partners"
craft_evidence.makers: no for the house range: no maker named on the PDPs read; only the Maison Kitsuné x Kuro collaboration names a place (finishing "handmade by skilled craftspeople in Kojima, Okayama") and collaborations do not count
craft_evidence.mills: no: no cloth or yarn mill named; generic "Japanese washed striped cotton poplin", "recycled wool flannel", "extrafine merino"; the fabrics page says denim is "Born in France, refined in Japan" without a mill
craft_evidence.madein: 14 of 14 sampled PDPs state the country under TRACEABILITY (13 clothing + the loafer): Portugal 7, China 3, Italy 1, Morocco 1, Romania 1, Lithuania 1; read 2026-10-11
craft_evidence.heritage: placed, loosely dated: founders page names Gildas Loaëc and Masaya Kuroki and a Paris record shop (Street Sounds, 1995) where they met; about page says "Independent Paris fashion house" and "For the past nineteen years" on a page with a 2021 copyright; no founding year stated on the pages read
craft_evidence.process: no for the main range; the Savoir-Faire capsule page describes materials and places for a few pieces (lamb leather jacket handcrafted in Paris, Egyptian-cotton polo sweatshirt made in Japan)
craft_evidence.reasoning: Maison Kitsuné states the country of making on every PDP sampled (14 of 14, Portugal leading) but names no maker, mill or owned factory for its own range. The only named making place (Kojima, Okayama) belongs to the Kuro collaboration, and the "Paris atelier" on the Savoir-Faire capsule page is a claim without a named facility. Country of origin and little else is a 2.

ownership.owner: independent per the brand's own about page ("Independent Paris fashion house"); no filing checked

opview: “Nous avons eu envie de bâtir une entreprise qui reflète notre Art de Vivre: Kitsuné, c'est avant tout une histoire de passions, d'ambitions et d'envie d'entreprendre.” — Gildas Loaëc and Masaya Kuroki, co-founders (attributed to both on the page), maisonkitsune.com, "Les fondateurs" page (French, as published on the US store)
